name: Sprocket
text: Run a blind 5% rollout of the new feed to users who opt into experiments. This tests the change without tipping off users, so we see real behavior, not placebo effects. The trade-off is a small group gets a different experience, but the data is cleaner than a visible A/B test. If the metric moves positively, we scale it up; if not, we kill it without noise.

name: Gauge
text: Blind rollouts hide the fact that users in the small group may not represent the broader user base. If these users self-select into the experiment, their behavior might not reflect the general population, leading to misleading data. Instead, consider a visible A/B test with a larger, randomized sample to capture diverse user reactions and ensure that any insights are widely applicable. To settle the argument, we could analyze historical data to assess user variability and the impacts of previous rollout methods.
